title: Highest deletions in BJP’s UP strongholds, new draft voter roll shows
shows: Ayush Tiwari compares the electors in each of Uttar Pradesh's assembly constituencies as the Commission published them for the 2024 Lok Sabha election with the draft roll of the summary revision of 17 November 2026, as s1d labs digitised and published it. By Scroll's count the electorate fell by 12% on average since 2024, by 12.9% on average in the 162 assembly segments where the BJP led in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and 10.7% in the 183 where the Samajwadi Party led, and of the 25 segments with the largest falls the BJP led in 20, the Congress in four and the Samajwadi Party in one. Scroll gives the largest fall as 34.4% in Allahabad North, followed by 34.3% in Lucknow Cantonment. It writes that these 25 segments are almost all urban, in cities such as Allahabad, Lucknow, Agra and Kanpur, which it shows from the areas the 2008 delimitation order gives them, and that the 25 with the smallest falls are mostly rural, with the Samajwadi Party leading in 13, the BJP in 11 and the Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) in one. It sets the figures beside the Chief Minister's remark at a party meeting in December 2025, as Scroll quotes it, that 90 per cent of four crore missing voters were the BJP's, and beside explanations that BJP functionaries gave other papers, that urban voters moved to their rural addresses and that students left the cities where they had enrolled.
quote: Our analysis shows that of the 25 assembly constituencies that saw the largest deletions of voters, the BJP finished first in 20 during the Lok Sabha polls.

For this analysis, Scroll compared the draft SSR roll released on November 17, which has been digitised and published by S1d Labs, with the assembly constituency-wise data of electors released by the poll body in 2024.
note: First reading, 27 November 2026, of the page fetched with curl and read in full from its markup. The page gives datePublished 2026-11-27T06:30:00+05:30 and carries no isAccessibleForFree field, and the whole text was in the page. Every figure is Scroll's, and the comparison is of net change between two rolls, which Scroll calls deletions. It sets the 2024 electors against the summary revision's draft, so the names added by Form 6 after the intensive revision, which Scroll puts at nearly 19 lakh from the Chief Electoral Officer's statement of 17 November, are already inside the second figure. Scroll's own figures for the intensive revision, more than 2 crore names removed or about 13.4% of the electorate, are given in the piece as background and are not carried. The 'lead' in a segment is the party that finished first there in the 2024 Lok Sabha count. Scroll's text names the Deputy Chief Minister as the member for Lucknow Cantonment, and gives the quotations of functionaries from The Indian Express, The Wire and ThePrint and of the BJP member for Agra Cantonment, and these are not carried beyond the summary. The party figures and the Chief Minister's remark are as Scroll reports them and are attributed. The s1d labs data is round 54 and Aman Bhargava's reading of the same rolls is round 55.
